author: Vox
description:
Black student enrollment has dropped at the top 50 most selective universities in the US. For example, prior to the end of race-based affirmative action in 2023, Black students made up 18% of the freshman class at Harvard; for the class of 2029, they’ll only be 11.5% of the student body. 

But this shift in where students are attending college has also led to a modern HBCU renaissance. Historically Black colleges and universities are seeing record-breaking applications.

description:
In the race to become Texas’ next senator, Republican candidate Ken Paxton and his surrogates have leaned into a specific line of attack on Democrat James Talarcio. From calling him “low-T” to “Tofu Talarico” — they want this campaign to be a referendum on manliness. 

On the Today, Explained podcast, we head to Texas to ask: What does it mean to be a good man in politics?

description:
Medical providers across the country are feeling the consequences of the One Big Beautiful Bill’s Medicaid budget cuts. The law won’t take effect until 2027, but Republicans are already dealing with the backlash. Vox’s Rachel Booth explains how the cuts could lead to fewer services and higher health care costs — even for people who keep their insurance.

author: Vox
description:
What does the country lose when one generation refuses to yield power?

Subscribe to our channel! http://goo.gl/0bsAjO

In this episode, Vox host Jonquilyn Hill talks with Idrees Kahloon, staff writer at the Atlantic, about why he believes America has become a gerontocracy – a government whose rulers are older than the rest of the population. There’s the age of political leaders in Congress and the White House. And there’s also the economic impact of having Americans over the age of 55 holding nearly three-quarters of the nation's wealth.

Jonquilyn and Idrees examine how this demographic and economic shift came to pass over the last several decades. They get into the political taboo over reforming Social Security and Medicare, the impact of housing market restrictions and zoning on younger home buyers, and the ways that government spending heavily favors older voters.

Guest Host: Jonquilyn Hill, host of Explain It To Me
Guest: Idrees Kahloon, Staff writer, The Atlantic
